title: John Chapter 2 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on John chapter 2 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: John Chapter 2 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of John Chapter 2.

questions.question: In John 2, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The ruler of the feast tasting the wine
questions.explanation: The marriage in Cana is mentioned first in John 2:1.

questions.question: Where was the marriage that Jesus attended?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the marriage took place in Cana of Galilee (John 2:1).

questions.question: Who was present at the marriage in Cana?
questions.explanation: The mother of Jesus is specifically mentioned as being there (John 2:1).

questions.question: What did the mother of Jesus say when they wanted wine?
questions.explanation: The mother of Jesus stated, 'They have no wine' (John 2:3).

questions.question: How did Jesus respond to his mother’s concern about the wine?
options: He said it was not his time
questions.correctAnswer: He said it was not his time
questions.explanation: Jesus replied, 'mine hour is not yet come' (John 2:4).

questions.question: What did the mother of Jesus instruct the servants to do?
options: Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it
questions.correctAnswer: Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it
questions.explanation: She instructed them to do whatever Jesus said (John 2:5).

questions.question: How many waterpots were there at the marriage?
questions.explanation: The text states that there were six waterpots of stone (John 2:6).

questions.question: What did Jesus tell the servants to do with the waterpots?
questions.explanation: Jesus instructed them to fill the waterpots with water (John 2:7).

questions.question: What did the servants do after Jesus told them to fill the waterpots?
options: They filled them up to the brim
questions.correctAnswer: They filled them up to the brim
questions.explanation: The servants filled the waterpots up to the brim (John 2:7).

questions.question: Who tasted the water that was made wine?
questions.explanation: The ruler of the feast tasted the water that was made wine (John 2:9).

questions.question: Did the ruler of the feast know where the wine came from?
questions.explanation: The ruler did not know whence it was, but the servants who drew the water knew (John 2:9).

questions.question: True or False: Jesus was called to the marriage.
questions.explanation: The text states that both Jesus and his disciples were called to the marriage (John 2:2).

questions.question: True or False: The waterpots were made of glass.
questions.explanation: The waterpots were made of stone, as stated in the text (John 2:6).

questions.question: True or False: The bridegroom was the first to taste the wine.
questions.explanation: The ruler of the feast, not the bridegroom, tasted the wine first (John 2:9).

questions.question: True or False: Jesus turned water into grape juice.
questions.explanation: The text states that Jesus turned water into wine, not grape juice (John 2:9).

medium.title: John Chapter 2 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from John Chapter 2 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did the governor of the feast say about the wine served at the wedding?
options: Every man at the beginning doth set forth good wine
The wine is of poor quality
questions.correctAnswer: Every man at the beginning doth set forth good wine
questions.explanation: This is stated in John 2:10, where the governor comments on the quality of the wine served at the feast.

questions.question: What does John 2:5 promise will happen if someone does what verse 2:5 commands?
options: They will receive the best wine
They will be rewarded for their obedience
questions.explanation: John 2:5 shows that obedience to Jesus leads to witnessing His power, as demonstrated in the subsequent miracle.

questions.question: What did Jesus do after the miracle at the wedding in Cana?
questions.explanation: John 2:12 indicates that after the miracle, Jesus and His family went to Capernaum, and then to Jerusalem.

questions.question: What does John 2:14 reveal about the temple when Jesus arrived?
options: It was being used for commerce
questions.correctAnswer: It was being used for commerce
questions.explanation: John 2:14 describes how Jesus found merchants and money changers in the temple, indicating it was being misused.

questions.question: What action did Jesus take against those selling in the temple?
questions.explanation: In John 2:15, Jesus made a scourge and drove out all the merchants and animals from the temple.

questions.question: According to John 2:17, what did the disciples remember about Jesus' actions in the temple?
options: The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up
He is the Son of God
questions.correctAnswer: The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up
questions.explanation: John 2:17 references a scripture that reflects Jesus' passionate defense of the temple as His Father's house.

questions.question: What question did the Jews ask Jesus after He cleared the temple?
questions.explanation: John 2:18 records the Jews questioning Jesus about the sign of His authority after His actions in the temple.

questions.question: How does John 2:11 describe the significance of the miracle at Cana?
options: It was the first miracle of Jesus
It was a sign of His power
It caused many to follow Him
questions.correctAnswer: It was the first miracle of Jesus
questions.explanation: John 2:11 states that this was the beginning of miracles Jesus performed, showcasing His glory.

questions.question: What does John 2:16 indicate about the purpose of the temple?
options: It is a place of worship
It is a house of merchandise
It should be a political center
questions.correctAnswer: It is a place of worship
questions.explanation: In John 2:16, Jesus emphasizes that the temple should not be treated as a marketplace but rather as His Father's house.

questions.question: What was the reaction of Jesus' disciples to His first miracle?
questions.explanation: John 2:11 indicates that the miracle led the disciples to believe in Jesus' divinity and power.

questions.question: What lesson can be learned from John 2:5 about obedience?
options: Obedience is only for the weak
questions.explanation: John 2:5 shows that following Jesus' instructions leads to a miraculous outcome, illustrating the importance of obedience.

questions.question: According to John 2:13, why did Jesus go up to Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: John 2:13 mentions that the Passover was at hand, prompting Jesus to go to Jerusalem.

questions.question: Is it true that Jesus expressed anger towards the commercial activities in the temple?
questions.explanation: True, as seen in John 2:15, where Jesus drove out the merchants, indicating His anger towards commercial activities in His Father's house.

questions.question: Is it true that the miracle at Cana was the last miracle Jesus performed?
questions.explanation: False, as the miracle at Cana was the first of many miracles Jesus performed during His ministry, as stated in John 2:11.

questions.question: Is it true that John 2:18 records Jesus performing a miracle?
questions.explanation: False, John 2:18 records the Jews questioning Jesus about His authority, not a miracle.

hard.title: John Chapter 2 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from John Chapter 2.

questions.question: What did Jesus say would happen if the temple were destroyed in John 2:19?
options: In three days I will raise it up
It will be rebuilt in forty-six years
questions.correctAnswer: In three days I will raise it up
questions.explanation: John 2:19 records Jesus saying, 'Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up,' indicating a prophecy about resurrection.

questions.question: How long did the Jews say the temple had been in building according to John 2:20?
questions.explanation: John 2:20 states the Jews said, 'Forty and six years was this temple in building,' highlighting the temple's long construction period.

questions.question: To what was Jesus referring when he spoke of the temple in John 2:21?
questions.explanation: John 2:21 clarifies that Jesus was speaking 'of the temple of his body,' indicating a typological reference to his resurrection.

questions.question: What caused the disciples to believe the scripture and Jesus' words according to John 2:22?
options: When Jesus was risen from the dead
When the money changers were expelled
questions.correctAnswer: When Jesus was risen from the dead
questions.explanation: John 2:22 states the disciples remembered Jesus' words 'when therefore he was risen from the dead,' leading to their belief.

questions.question: Why did Jesus not commit himself unto many who believed in John 2:24?
options: Because they were not true believers
Because he was afraid of the Jews
Because he was not ready to reveal himself
questions.explanation: John 2:24 explains Jesus 'did not commit himself unto them, because he knew all men,' indicating his discernment of human nature.

questions.question: What did Jesus not need, according to John 2:25, to know what was in man?
options: That any should testify of man
questions.correctAnswer: That any should testify of man
questions.explanation: John 2:25 states Jesus 'needed not that any should testify of man: for he knew what was in man,' emphasizing his divine insight.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'ναός' (naos) in John 2:19 mean?
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'ναός' (naos) used in John 2:19 specifically refers to the inner sanctuary or temple building itself, not the entire precinct.

questions.question: Which literary technique is primarily used in Jesus' statement in John 2:19 about destroying and raising the temple?
questions.explanation: John 2:19 uses typology, where the temple represents Jesus' body, foreshadowing his death and resurrection.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is echoed by Jesus' zeal for the temple in John 2:17?
questions.explanation: John 2:17 quotes Psalm 69:9: 'The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up,' connecting Jesus' zeal to this Old Testament passage.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage connects with Jesus' prophecy about the temple and resurrection in John 2:19-21?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:4 affirms the resurrection of Jesus on the third day, fulfilling the prophecy in John 2:19-21 about raising the temple, his body.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes Jesus driving out the money changers from the temple in John 2?
options: Jesus went up to Jerusalem for the Passover
Jesus performed the water to wine miracle
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus went up to Jerusalem for the Passover
questions.explanation: John 2:13 states 'And the Jews' passover was at hand, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem,' which immediately precedes the temple cleansing.

questions.question: What is the literary device used in John 2:11 where Jesus' miracle is called 'the beginning of miracles'?
questions.explanation: John 2:11 uses 'incipit' as it marks the beginning or opening of Jesus' public miracles, introducing his glory.

questions.question: How does the cleansing of the temple in John 2:15 function as a typological act?
options: It symbolizes Jesus purifying the worship of God
It shows Jesus' rejection of the law
It is a sign of economic reform
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes Jesus purifying the worship of God
questions.explanation: John 2:15 shows Jesus making a scourge and driving out merchants, symbolizing purification of the temple worship, a typological act for spiritual cleansing.

questions.question: What cultural significance did the waterpots have in the miracle at Cana according to John 2:6?
options: They were used for Jewish purification rites
They held sacred oil for anointing
They were containers for wine storage
They were idols worshiped by the people
questions.correctAnswer: They were used for Jewish purification rites
questions.explanation: John 2:6 specifies that the six waterpots were 'after the manner of the purifying of the Jews,' used for ceremonial washing.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus committed himself fully to those who believed in him after the miracles in John 2:23.
questions.explanation: John 2:24 states that Jesus 'did not commit himself unto them, because he knew all men,' showing restraint despite their belief.

theological.title: John Chapter 2 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from John Chapter 2 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does John 2:4 teach about the timing and sovereignty of Christ's redemptive mission?
options: Christ acts only according to the Father's sovereign timing
Christ acts independently of the Father’s will
Christ’s mission is self-determined without divine plan
Christ’s miracles are random acts without purpose
questions.correctAnswer: Christ acts only according to the Father's sovereign timing
questions.explanation: John 2:4 shows Jesus saying, 'mine hour is not yet come,' indicating His obedience to the Father's appointed time for His redemptive work.

questions.question: What doctrine about Christ’s knowledge of human nature is taught in John 2:25?
options: Christ possesses divine omniscience regarding human hearts
Christ is limited in understanding human motives
Christ relies on human testimony to know mankind
Christ is unaware of humanity’s innermost thoughts
questions.correctAnswer: Christ possesses divine omniscience regarding human hearts
questions.explanation: John 2:25 states Jesus 'knew what was in man,' affirming His divine attribute of omniscience concerning human nature.

questions.question: What doctrine about Jesus’ role as the initiator of faith is taught in John 2:11?
options: Jesus manifests His glory so that disciples believe in Him
Faith in Jesus arises apart from His works
Miracles cause disbelief among His followers
Glory is unrelated to faith in the Gospels
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus manifests His glory so that disciples believe in Him
questions.explanation: John 2:11 notes this miracle was the 'beginning' that manifested Jesus’ glory, leading His disciples to believe, highlighting His role in initiating faith.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does John 2:24 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: John 2:24 reveals Jesus did not commit Himself to many because 'he knew all men,' demonstrating His divine omniscience.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is specifically demonstrated by Jesus’ zeal in John 2:17?
questions.explanation: John 2:17 cites 'The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up,' showing Jesus’ holy zeal for the purity of the Father’s house.

questions.question: How does the cleansing of the temple in John 2:15 connect to the Old Testament prophetic theme of purifying the worship of God?
options: It fulfills the prophecy of Malachi regarding pure offerings
It contradicts the Old Testament temple practices
It introduces a new system of temple commerce
It symbolizes the abolition of Jewish law
questions.correctAnswer: It fulfills the prophecy of Malachi regarding pure offerings
questions.explanation: The cleansing aligns with prophetic calls (e.g., Malachi 3:1-3) for purity in worship, showing Jesus’ role in fulfilling purification themes.

questions.question: How does Jesus’ reference to raising 'this temple' in three days (John 2:19) prefigure the resurrection theme found elsewhere in Scripture?
options: It prefigures His resurrection as the new temple
It refers only to the physical temple in Jerusalem
It denies any resurrection after death
It predicts the temple’s destruction by Roman soldiers
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures His resurrection as the new temple
questions.explanation: John 2:19-21 clarifies Jesus spoke of His body as the temple, prefiguring His resurrection, fulfilling the typology of the temple as God’s dwelling (cf. Ezekiel 37).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do John 2:3 and John 2:5 teach about Jesus’ role in salvation and human obedience?
options: Jesus initiates salvation and humans must respond in obedience
Salvation is achieved solely by human effort without Jesus’ intervention
Jesus passively observes human sin without acting
Human obedience is irrelevant to salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus initiates salvation and humans must respond in obedience
questions.explanation: John 2:3 shows the problem (no wine), and John 2:5 records Mary telling servants to do whatever Jesus commands, illustrating divine initiative and human submission.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do John 2:18 and John 2:22 teach about Jesus’ signs and the scriptural witness to His resurrection?
options: Jesus’ miracles and resurrection fulfill Scripture, authenticating His messianic identity
Jesus’ signs are unrelated to Scripture
The resurrection is a later legend with no scriptural basis
Scripture contradicts Jesus’ miracles and resurrection
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus’ miracles and resurrection fulfill Scripture, authenticating His messianic identity
questions.explanation: John 2:18 asks for a sign; 2:22 explains the resurrection fulfilled Jesus’ words and Scripture, affirming His identity.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do John 2:13-16 and John 2:17 teach about Jesus’ zeal for God’s holiness and judgment on corrupted worship?
options: Jesus’ zeal demonstrates His holiness and judgment against commercializing worship
Jesus condones the temple commerce as acceptable
Jesus’ actions indicate indifference to temple purity
Jesus supports the exploitation of worshippers
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus’ zeal demonstrates His holiness and judgment against commercializing worship
questions.explanation: John 2:13-16 narrates Jesus cleansing the temple, and 2:17 references the Psalm about zeal for God’s house, showing His holy judgment.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Jesus’ miracle at Cana was just a natural event or later embellishment. What does John 2:7-11 actually teach?
options: The miracle was a genuine sign revealing Jesus’ glory and divine authority
The event was a common wedding custom without supernatural elements
The water-to-wine story is symbolic but never actually occurred
The miracle was performed by the servants, not Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: The miracle was a genuine sign revealing Jesus’ glory and divine authority
questions.explanation: John 2:7-11 presents Jesus’ turning water into wine as His first miracle, manifesting His glory and causing disciples to believe, affirming its historic and theological reality.

questions.question: What doctrine about Jesus’ interrelation with His family and disciples is evident in John 2:12?
options: Jesus maintains close relational ties while advancing His public ministry
Jesus rejects all family and disciples after the first miracle
Jesus isolates Himself completely for ministry
Jesus only associates with His family, not disciples
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus maintains close relational ties while advancing His public ministry
questions.explanation: John 2:12 shows Jesus going down to Capernaum with His mother, brethren, and disciples, evidencing relational continuity amid ministry.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is manifested in Jesus’ ability to transform water into wine in John 2:7-9?
questions.explanation: The miracle in John 2:7-9 demonstrates Jesus’ sovereign power to alter natural elements, underscoring His divine authority over creation.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do John 2:23 and John 2:24 teach about human response to Jesus’ miracles and His divine discernment of faith?
options: Many believed because of miracles, but Jesus did not entrust Himself to all due to His divine discernment
All who saw miracles were automatically saved
Miracles caused universal rejection of Jesus
Jesus lacked knowledge about human faith
questions.correctAnswer: Many believed because of miracles, but Jesus did not entrust Himself to all due to His divine discernment
questions.explanation: John 2:23 shows many believed on Jesus’ name due to miracles; 2:24 states Jesus did not commit Himself to them because He knew human hearts.

questions.question: How does John 2:6 reflect the Jewish cultural and religious context in which Jesus performed His first miracle?
options: The six waterpots were used for Jewish purification rites, showing Jesus’ respect for religious customs
The waterpots were ordinary vessels with no religious significance
Jesus rejected Jewish purification customs entirely
The waterpots were symbolic of Gentile worship practices
questions.correctAnswer: The six waterpots were used for Jewish purification rites, showing Jesus’ respect for religious customs
questions.explanation: John 2:6 specifies the waterpots were 'after the manner of the purifying of the Jews,' indicating Jesus’ engagement with Jewish ritual purity.
